medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The Office of Student Engagement (OSE) is here to support you throughout your medical school journey. We provide an array of services, resources, and opportunities to help you make the most of your experience and pursue your goals successfully. We are committed to facilitating a positive learning environment that promotes a sense of belonging, holistic well-being, leadership development, and a supportive community. Our goal is to ensure that you don't wait to graduate from medical school to enjoy life.

To Learn more about our support programs, please visit our website: https://medschool.kp.org/student-life/student-engagement
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Participating in a KPSOM student organization can help students to develop leadership skills, build community, and create professional connections with faculty and staff advisers. Get involved, meet students with shared interests, take part in programs and events, and enhance your medical school experience by joining organizations that match your interests. 

KPSOM has three types of student organizations based on affinity, personal interest (academic, professional, social, etc.), and medical specialty. New and different organizations are formed on an ongoing basis. The school also has campus-wide committees that are led by various department staff, and enable students to address issues affecting the entire KPSOM community.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Our medical education building is located in Pasadena, California, only 10 miles from downtown Los Angeles. Our progressive city is highly walkable and bike-friendly, with palm trees and a warm and sunny climate year-round.

Your time in medical school will account for some of the most rewarding, exhilarating, and challenging years of your life. It will test you and stretch you in many ways, while preparing you to care for patients, advocate on their behalf, and heal communities.

The Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine places a high priority on supporting your well-being, so that you can thrive throughout your four years. You'll have access to a comprehensive network of support to ensure you find the help you need, when you need it.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine Outlist consists of students, faculty, and staff who identify as LGBTQ+.

We envision the KPSOM Outlist as a tool to develop community amongst those who identify as LGBTQ+, and bring visibility to the LGBTQ+ members of our school’s community. We would like for the Outlist to generate connections, foster mentorship conversations, and celebrate the many LGBTQ+ contributors at our school.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
At Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine, we welcome students from all backgrounds and with various life experiences, including those who have or may develop a disability.

The school abides by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

To learn more about our resources for disabled students, please visit our website: https://medschool.kp.org/student-life/support-for-disabled-students
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Students will have access to academic advising and support, mental health counseling, and workshops on topics such as stress management and test anxiety. Developing resilience skills is part of the required curriculum. The school places such a high priority on helping students develop into healthy, resilient physician leaders that, throughout your four years here, time will be dedicated to participating in purposeful, formative exercises that support your personal and professional development. 

These quarterly sessions are called REACH (Reflection, Education, Assessment, Coaching, and Health and well-being) weeks. All students will also be paired with a physician coach, who will be your confidant and guide, helping you set attainable goals and navigate the challenges of medical school. Coaches are resources to help you form a robust professional identity as you reflect on your experiences and establish goals.

The school has several amenities that make it easy to fit exercise into your busy life as a student. Students will have access to a yoga studio, meditation spaces, a fitness center, and healthy food options at our Pasadena building. The surrounding area features walking trails connecting you to Pasadena, which is both highly walkable and bike-friendly. Third- and fourth-year students will also have access to fitness centers at their clinical training locations.

Everyone experiences difficult life events and challenges that may affect their well-being. The pressures of medical school can make these challenges even greater, and students may need support throughout their four years at KPSOM. We are fortunate as a medical school to be able to provide services to support students’ overall mental health and well-being.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Your time in medical school will account for some of the most rewarding, exhilarating, and challenging years of your life. It will test you and stretch you in many ways, while preparing you to care for patients, advocate on their behalf, and heal communities.

The Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine places a high priority on supporting your well-being and resilience, so that you can thrive throughout your four years. You'll have access to a comprehensive network of support to ensure you find the help you need, when you need it.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms:
You’ll find the support you need to succeed here, including:
Academic advising and tutoring

medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students start interacting with patients within the first weeks of medical school. These clinical experiences will be conducted at one of the six Kaiser Permanente medical centers in Los Angeles.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Throughout all four years, your education is integrated within a case-based, spiral progression that lets you return to key educational information and concepts over time in increasing complexity.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students at Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine will begin clinical rotations in the first year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Our students are expected to meet the same standards of professionalism as all healthcare providers, including punctual and regular attendance for all academic and clinical responsibilities.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Our curriculum begins with an Early Immersive Experience in Year 1 and ends with residency preparation in Year 4. These components bookend coursework integrating Foundational, Clinical, and Health Systems Science with opportunities to apply knowledge and gain skills through academic experiences such as Longitudinal Integrated Clerkships (LICs), inpatient immersion, selectives and electives, longitudinal service-learning, and a scholarly project. You will learn core skills by following panels of patients and their communities over time, while maintaining one-on-one relationships with a preceptor. Students observe patients and communities through the entire care continuum, including diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.

Wellness is an important curricular element at Kaiser Permanente School of Medicine. Over the four years of medical school, students will participate in learning series called REACH (Reflection, Education, Assessment, Coaching, Health, and well-being.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: At the Kaiser Permanente School of Medicine, we endeavor to train our students to become doctors, leaders and advocates in the specialty area of their choice. We are cognizant of the shortages in both primary care and specialty care. Our students will be well equipped to train in primary care and specialty residency programs throughout the country.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Our faculty and students pursue a wide range of innovative scholarly work. We connect our students with mentored research opportunities that build on our curriculum to help them both critically assess and produce the evidence that informs healthcare. Our research leverages the health plan members that Kaiser Permanente serves, while forging partnerships with our communities and external collaborations with researchers in Southern California and beyond.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Education is integrated within a case-based, spiral progression that returns to key educational information and concepts in increasing complexity, so knowledge and skills evolve simultaneously.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: We believe that service learning offers our students an essential opportunity to augment classroom learning with skills and knowledge you can best learn working with people where they live.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Each student will meaningfully explore an area of interest as they complete a scholarly project under the close guidance of a faculty member. Students access the Kaiser Permanente research enterprise.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Phase 1 courses (Integrated Sciences, LIC, and REACH) are pass/fail. In Phase 2, Integrated Sciences and REACH are pass/fail; Phase 2 LIC and Phase 3 Clinical Experiences are graded on a tiered basis.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
This is a medical school for students whose scientific curiosity is matched by a strong sense of mission. You’ll learn to advocate for better health in homes, schools, workplaces, and society at large. 

Lectures in basic sciences for the first two years, clinical sciences the third and fourth years—you’ll study biomedical science, clinical science, and a third discipline, health systems science (which explores how human relationships influence health), across all four years. 

The school was designed with an eye toward the future. It's ready to accommodate the latest technologies, facilitate student collaboration and well-being, and house evolving best practices in education.

Our medical education building is located in Pasadena, California, only 10 miles from downtown Los Angeles. Our progressive city is highly walkable and bike-friendly, with palm trees and a warm and sunny climate year-round.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine strives to provide a world-class education for every one of our students.

We aim to ignite a passion for lifelong learning, a desire to serve patients, and an unwavering commitment to improve the health and well-being of communities.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants admitted October 2026 – April 2027 have until May 30, 2026 to make their decision about matriculation. Applicants are given 5 business days to respond to offers made after April 30
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Letters of recommendation must be signed and on official letterhead.

In particular, letters of recommendation should evaluate one or more of the following:

Collaborative teamwork skills
Communication skills 
Creativity and resourcefulness 
Critical thinking and problem-solving skills
Demonstrated leadership potential 
Integrity and moral standards
Intellectual curiosity 
Passion for medicine and healthcare 
Persistence and resilience 
Reliability and accountability 
Responsiveness to feedback 
Self-awareness
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
As part of the Primary Application via AMCAS, all applicants are required to submit letters of recommendation, which assists us in the assessment of your promise as a medical student.

You can submit letters in one of two ways:

1. One committee letter that integrates comments from multiple recommenders, authored by a pre-health committee or pre-health advisor

2. Three to six individual letters submitted by three professionals familiar with your academic performance and personal attributes
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: We believe that the interview day is a critical part of our assessment and selection process, as it gives us an opportunity to get to know you better. It also provides you a better sense of who we are and allows you an opportunity to get your questions answered. We will utilize a hybrid model, consisting of the Multiple Mini Interview and a traditional interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: We will utilize a hybrid model, consisting of Multiple Mini Interviews and a traditional interview.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews will be virtual for the 2026 - 2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Once we've received the Primary Application, we'll invite all eligible applicants to complete the school's Secondary Application. You'll also be able to monitor your status on our application portal.

medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Coursework taken in Canada will be accepted. At this time, the school is able to accept applications only from U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and DACA recipients.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine's admissions philosophy emphasizes a mission-aligned view of our applicants. As such, your academic achievements are always considered in relation to your experiences, milestones, and personal attributes. We believe this approach allows us to create a multidimensional portrait of each applicant, while admitting a class that embodies the school's commitment to innovation, academic rigor, service, and inclusive excellence.

Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine will accept Pass/Fail grades, without prejudice, for courses taken by applicants during the COVID-19 pandemic. It has always been the school’s practice to consider grades in the context of numerous other aspects of the application, and an international crisis certainly provides a unique and compelling context. In making this statement, we understand that some undergraduate schools are allowing students to take courses either for a grade or on a Pass/Fail basis. 

MCAT: Please visit the AAMC website for the MCAT Calendar, Scheduling Deadlines, and Score Release Dates.  https://students-residents.aamc.org/applying-medical-school/article/mcat-testing-calendar-score-release-dates

The school will accept online coursework taken in spring, summer, and fall 2020, as well as spring and fall 2021. We do not recommend taking all prerequisite courses through online coursework. Please note that online bachelor’s degrees will not be considered in the application process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
We require all applicants to submit their MCAT scores. 

You must take the MCAT no later than September 2026. 
For the 2026-2027 application cycle, the school considers MCAT scores dating back to July 2024.

However, know that your test scores will be considered in the full context of your application.

medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of intent will be accepted from April 30 to May 30.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: To ensure that you are equipped to complete our program, we will ask you to sign a set of technical standards as you enter the school. Our Catalog explains these standards. They cover general functions, cognitive ability, social attributes, and more.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Starting with the 2027 entering class and beyond, Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine will begin charging tuition for the MD program. Our commitment to delivering a valuable and enriching educational experience remains unwavering, and we are dedicated to supporting future students as our institution evolves. KPSOM will provide debt-free, need-based institutional aid that can cover each student’s demonstrated financial need, helping to minimize or eliminate reliance on medical school loans. For more details, please visit our website. Thank you for considering KPSOM for your medical education; we look forward to receiving your application.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Students at Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine will have the opportunity to acquire additional degrees to further prepare them to becomes scientists, leaders and advocates. Through a partnership with Caltech, students will be able to obtain an MD-PhD, and through partnerships with the University of California, Los Angeles, and the University of Southern California, they can obtain a Master of Public Health, and a Master of Health Administration. Students can also earn an MBA through our partnership with Pepperdine University and a Master of Science in Clinical Informatics from Stanford University.
